content:
This image shows a page from what appears to be a theater program or literature analysis in French. The text begins with a quote from Norman Mailer about Kennedy, stating that "a man who attains power becomes a machine."

The main content discusses the play "Bérénice," analyzing its themes of heartbreaking separation and the eternal story of a man who gives up intimate happiness for honor and reputation. There's a reference to Shakespeare's "Othello" with a quote from Cassio about losing "the immortal part of myself."

The text explores the character of Titus as a potential dictator who makes the decision to exile the woman he loves, fulfilling his tragic destiny as a man seeking eternity.

At the bottom of the page, there's production information indicating this was a co-production between Théâtre du Gymnase-Marseille and several other French theaters including Théâtre national de Chaillot and Festival d'Avignon. It notes the show's duration (2:05) and appears to include performance dates at the "Cloître des Carmes" venue.

The page has reference numbers (2,28) in the top right corner.
